provenance: Factory baseline. The critical-package list comes from recorded failure scenarios; the coverage list comes from our own measurement records. How many runs each card has, and where they ran, stay in the private archive.
provenance_grammar_note: Every tested_gpus entry carries `measured YYYY-MM-DD`, the day that card first appears in our own run records. It is an anchor, not a story: the date resolves to one batch in our measurement ledger, and everything about that batch -- how many runs, which hosts, what it cost -- stays there and never travels with this file. A guard refuses any entry whose anchor resolves to no batch.
confidence_note: high = the verdict rests on a large body of runs; low = we have run this card, but only a few times. The counting rule lives in scripts/propose-tested-gpus.py.
critical_packages_note: Packages whose exact version decides whether a rebuilt environment runs at all: compiled extensions, anything bound to a CUDA line, and the ones whose ABI moves between minor releases. The fingerprint records their versions so a rebuild can be compared against the machine that worked. The list came out of real failures, not from reading changelogs -- each name is here because a mismatch on it broke a run. The same list is mirrored in fingerprint.py as CRITICAL_PACKAGES, the copy used when this file cannot be read.
